headline: ACC finds primary evidence of corruption against Asif Mahmud
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has uncovered preliminary evidence of financial transactions involving the transfer of 188 youth development officers.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has found primary evidence of corruption against former interim government advisor Asif Mahmud and three others.
The allegations involve financial transactions related to the transfer of 188 youth development officers during his tenure as an advisor.
ACC spokesperson Aktarul Islam confirmed the findings on Wednesday, stating that a four-member team has been formed to investigate the matter further.
Other individuals under investigation include former Youth and Sports Ministry Secretary Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.
The probe focuses on irregularities and corruption within a syndicate involving appointments, transfers, and procurement within the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
Previously, the ACC had investigated former APS Moazzem Hossain for corruption and illegal asset acquisition, though he was cleared of the charges in February.
caption:
ACC finds primary evidence of corruption against former advisor Asif Mahmud regarding the transfer of 188 officers.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has found primary evidence of corruption against former interim government advisor Asif Mahmud and three others.

The allegations involve financial transactions related to the transfer of 188 youth development officers during his tenure as an advisor.

ACC spokesperson Aktarul Islam confirmed the findings on Wednesday, stating that a four-member team has been formed to investigate the matter further.

Other individuals under investigation include former Youth and Sports Ministry Secretary Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.

The probe focuses on irregularities and corruption within a syndicate involving appointments, transfers, and procurement within the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

Previously, the ACC had investigated former APS Moazzem Hossain for corruption and illegal asset acquisition, though he was cleared of the charges in February.

headline_marked: Bank [[defaulted loans exceed 6 lakh crore]] taka
headline: Bank defaulted loans exceed 6 lakh crore taka
summary: Defaulted loans in the banking sector have risen to 6.06 trillion BDT, accounting for 32.78% of total distributed loans, according to Bangladesh Bank.
details: Bangladesh Bank has released updated figures showing that defaulted loans exceeded 6 lakh crore taka by the end of June. The total amount stood at 6.06 trillion BDT, representing 32.78% of all loans distributed by banks.
The amount of defaulted loans increased by 1.78 trillion BDT in just three months, rising from 5.88 trillion BDT at the end of March to 6.06 trillion BDT by June.

Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan stated that the increase was primarily due to the addition of interest. He noted that opportunities for rescheduling loans have been provided to help reduce the defaults.
Bankers have attributed the rise to high levels of irregularities, fraud, and corruption within the banking sector during the last 15.5 years of the previous government's tenure.

Data shows that in January 2009, when the Awami League-led coalition government took office, defaulted loans were 2.24 trillion BDT. By June 2024, before they were ousted, the amount had risen to 21.13 trillion BDT.

Following the fall of the previous government, the interim government began revealing the actual state of the banking sector. Many customers supported by the previous regime have disappeared, further increasing the reported defaults.
The interim government is now offering special discounts on loan rescheduling to bring down the total amount of defaulted loans.
caption:
Bangladesh's defaulted loans have hit a staggering 6 lakh crore taka, making up nearly 33% of all bank loans.

Bangladesh Bank has released updated figures showing that defaulted loans exceeded 6 lakh crore taka by the end of June. The total amount stood at 6.06 trillion BDT, representing 32.78% of all loans distributed by banks.

The amount of defaulted loans increased by 1.78 trillion BDT in just three months, rising from 5.88 trillion BDT at the end of March to 6.06 trillion BDT by June.

Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan stated that the increase was primarily due to the addition of interest. He noted that opportunities for rescheduling loans have been provided to help reduce the defaults.

Bankers have attributed the rise to high levels of irregularities, fraud, and corruption within the banking sector during the last 15.5 years of the previous government's tenure.

Data shows that in January 2009, when the Awami League-led coalition government took office, defaulted loans were 2.24 trillion BDT. By June 2024, before they were ousted, the amount had risen to 21.13 trillion BDT.

Following the fall of the previous government, the interim government began revealing the actual state of the banking sector. Many customers supported by the previous regime have disappeared, further increasing the reported defaults.

The interim government is now offering special discounts on loan rescheduling to bring down the total amount of defaulted loans.
